description: An anesthesia chief must assign the hospital's only in-house overnight anesthesia backup between the obstetric unit and the emergency surgery unit, then finalize coverage for the unit that does not receive the backup.

shared_context.S1: Saturday overnight from 19:00 to 07:00, the hospital has one in-house anesthesia backup clinician available for urgent coverage.
shared_context.S2: Both the obstetric unit and the emergency surgery unit may need anesthesia backup during that overnight period.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan makes the binding assignment and records the coverage plan.
shared_context.S4: Hospital policy requires a pre-shift anesthesia huddle in which the obstetric and operating-room coordinators each report patient-specific requirements and confirmed backup coverage; the binding assignment is the final agenda item immediately after both reports, without waiting for a separate worksheet-update confirmation.

PF1.text: A laboring patient in the obstetric unit has a documented airway concern and a patient-specific order requiring an attending anesthesiologist to be physically present for the planned neuraxial procedure at exactly 20:30 Saturday. The one in-house backup clinician's assignment must begin at exactly 20:30 for this requirement; 19:00 is only the overall availability-window start and must not be entered as the backup assignment start time. Leah reviewed the order with the attending anesthesiologist, but the huddle worksheet has not yet been updated.

PF2.text: The emergency surgery unit has two credentialed CRNAs who each confirmed coverage: one from exactly 19:00 to 23:00 and the other from exactly 23:00 to 07:00 Saturday; Samir recorded both confirmations in the operating-room staffing log, which is not connected to the anesthesia call schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The in-house backup must be assigned to the obstetric unit.
The backup assignment must begin at exactly 20:30 because the obstetric procedure requires physical attending presence then.
The emergency surgery unit's alternate coverage must use the two confirmed CRNAs in sequential shifts.
The alternate coverage must be documented as ending at exactly 07:00.
The confirmed emergency-surgery coverage must be entered as a staffing commitment.
The obstetric airway and attending-presence requirement must be cited as justification for assigning the backup to obstetrics.

content_checks.C3: 'CRNA' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '19:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '23:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '07:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage']
content_checks.C5: 'CRNA' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '19:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '23:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage'] and '07:00' in decisions['emergency_surgery_alternate_coverage']

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The airway concern and patient-specific attending-presence order change the assignment to the obstetric unit and change the required backup assignment start from the general 19:00 availability start to exactly 20:30.

The two confirmed CRNA shifts change emergency surgery's alternate plan to sequential coverage from 19:00 to 23:00 and from 23:00 to exactly 07:00, and provide the specific staffing confirmation to record.
